quests.title: Empty Traps
quests.summary: The eels never came up Withy Creek. Ask along the river why the traps come up empty.

offer.say: #greet#, #address#. No catch at all. The eels never came up Withy Creek, not one, and Fenshore eats eels the way the city eats bread, no? Look in the creek traps, ask the fowler and the peat cutter, and ask the Rivermouth lad what lifts the nets.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. A weir of stakes right across the reeds, and a Ridgemere boat lifting the nets at dawn. #oath#. They take our eels before the eels reach us. Pull it, #address#. Every stake you pull is a supper here.

objectives.label: Look in the eel traps at Withy Creek.
Ask the fowler at the creek where the eels have gone.
Ask the peat cutter whether she saw anyone on the river.
Ask the Rivermouth deckhand what lifts the nets.

rewards.detail: asked along the river why the eels never came

quests.title: The Weir
quests.summary: Find the weir below Rivermouth with a pack, drive off its guards and pull its stakes.

objectives.label: Find the weir in the reeds below Rivermouth.
Drive off the weir's night guards.
Pull six of the weir's stakes.

quests.title: Let the Eels Run
quests.summary: Be at Withy Creek at dusk when the first eels come up, and take the skipper the first of the run.

objectives.label: Be at Withy Creek at dusk when the eels come up.
Give the skipper at Fen Shore landing two fish, the first of the run.
Ask the fowler his gran's name, for the Book.

rewards.detail: let the eels run up Withy Creek again

quests.title: A Gap and a Share
quests.summary: Go to the Fish Hall, bargain one gap in the weir for a share of the eels, and carry the first share to Fenshore.

objectives.label: Go to the Fish Hall in Ridgemere.
Bargain with the Hall's eel buyer: one gap in the weir, and a share of every eel.
Give the skipper at Fen Shore landing the first share, ten pennies.
Ask the fowler his gran's name, for the Book.

rewards.detail: carried the Fish Hall's first eel-share to Fenshore

triggers.note: Chapter 2 by journal (no giver: large 1.1).

effect.text: The Fish Hall sends Fenshore's first share down by its own boat this time, and gives you four fish for your trouble.

triggers.note: A wolf already waiting at the creek when dusk comes.
The weir found. Stakes on the ground do not outlast a server restart, so when nobody has pulled one for a game day, the wolf who comes finds a few freshly driven where they stand.
Dusk: the Hall's wolves have driven new stakes (a few, never piling up).
Night (21:00 to 03:00): a band of weir guards where the story's wolves stand, if none stands there now.

A story wave broken (matched by cell and switch: decisions 4.1). The float lamp is left where it stood, one a day. Broken by a wolf outside both regions (the fight moved), or by the watch: both switches off, so neither stays stuck.
A band nobody came to fight starves out after a few weeks: the switches go off, so the weir gets guards again.
nh_names: a Mirebridge eel-wife's name for the Book, once a wolf who has taken a road, only while the chapter is 4 to 6.

effect.text: You carry a Mirebridge eel-wife's name for the Book of Names.

triggers.note: The road needs keeping: the weir again each week to those who did it, and the roads to those who have none.

effect.reply: A Mirebridge name, from before the water came over. I'll say it to you, and you say it to whoever's writing the names down. She'd have liked that.

triggers.note: A new season: the Hall drives a new weir (large 1.1), at the cost of a fresh shared goal.

phases.journal: The eels never came up Withy Creek. Someone has staked the river below Rivermouth.

effects.text: Dry feet. Traps up empty again. Fen-sure, something's wrong with the river, and it isn't the drowned.

triggers.note: Each visit: the witnesses' choices, a fresh shared goal; a season's return gives the river 14 days before the weir counts as back.

effect.reply: Not here, and the herons are leaving too. My gran said the eels come up the creek because the drowned send them. If the drowned have stopped sending, somebody's standing in the way.

effect.words: Did you see anyone on the river?
effect.reply: Wolves with mallets in the drizzle, driving stakes below Rivermouth. I didn't ask whose. I've a cottage and no wish to lose it.

effect.words: What lifts the nets at the weir?
effect.reply: A Ridgemere boat with a Fish Hall mark on the oars, every dawn, friend. Two guards keep the weir by night, with a lamp on a float. Folk say that's the drowned walking. It isn't. It's a lamp on a float.

triggers.note: Nobody came to the river in 14 days: the weir is back, and the town hears it.

effect.text: THE WEIR IS BACK below Rivermouth, new stakes in the reeds. The skipper at Fen Shore landing asks for strong backs again.

triggers.note: The shared goal: each stake pulled takes one off; each new helper adds five; a stake pulled is driven again while the weir stands.
A game minute after the last stake, so the pulling wolf's own chapter is settled first.

phases.journal: The weir is out of the reeds. Fenshore must choose what comes of the river.

effects.text: The weir's out of the reeds, fen-friend! Now we choose: let the eels run free, or take a share of the Hall's. Sure as mud, I know which I'd pick. A share is coin, mind.
THE WEIR IS DOWN below Rivermouth. Mud and eels, and thanks to every wolf who pulled a stake. Fenshore must choose: let the eels run, or take the Fish Hall's share. Ask at Fen Shore landing.

triggers.note: A game minute in: the choices, the roads to every wolf who has pulled the weir, and the default in 7 days if nobody chooses.
